FATAL: payments pod cannot resolve postgres.prod.svc.cluster.local — DNS lookup timeout after 30s

The payments service operations runbook is a comprehensive guide for on-call engineers managing the payments microservice in the production Kubernetes cluster. It covers a wide range of standard operational tasks including but not limited to deployment procedures, rollback strategies, configuration management, and incident response protocols. When responding to alerts from the payments service, on-call engineers should first acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and then proceed to gather initial diagnostic information from the relevant monitoring dashboards. The primary dashboard for payments service health is hosted on Grafana and can be accessed via the corporate VPN. Common alerts that on-call engineers may encounter include high error rates, elevated latency, pod restarts, memory leaks, CPU throttling, and connection pool exhaustion. For each of these alert types, the runbook provides detailed troubleshooting steps and escalation procedures. In the event of a pod entering CrashLoopBackOff state, the recommended first step is to retrieve the pod logs using kubectl logs with the previous flag to see the logs from the last terminated container instance. The on-call engineer should look for any error messages or stack traces that may indicate the root cause of the crash. Common root causes include misconfigured environment variables, missing secrets, network connectivity issues to dependent services such as postgres or redis, out of memory conditions, and configuration drift between environments. If the pod is unable to reach its database, verify DNS resolution from within the cluster using a debug pod. The team lead is Alice and the secondary on-call is Bob. Pager rotation is weekly and follows the engineering schedule maintained in the team wiki. For escalations beyond the on-call team, contact the platform engineering group via the dedicated Slack channel. Postmortem documents for past incidents are stored in Confluence and should be reviewed periodically by all team members. The service-level objectives for the payments service include a 99.9% availability target and a p99 latency under 200ms. Compliance and audit requirements mandate that all production incidents be documented within 24 hours of resolution.
